A partial update.

regulator, and silently changing it would break the audit trail's link to a real
person. Correcting one is a deliberate, separate operation.

get.description:
The public key access tokens are signed with (RFC 7517).

For the Part B services, which verify tokens themselves instead of calling Part A on
every request. Public by design: it can verify a signature and nothing else.

The five metrics over a window (default: the last 30 days). Total Patients is the
register's size now, not a count over the window.
One point per day with data: Appointments Booked Over Time is `metric=booked`.

Department utilisation over a window (default: the last 30 days): of the slots each
department offered, how many hold an appointment. Busiest first.

post.description:
The paired write, and nothing else (D-16). The follow-up -- visit timer, refund,
waitlist -- is started by the `appointments.cancelled` consumer from the event this
transaction writes (Week 3 slice 4), so the request touches no Temporal at all and a
follow-up can no longer be lost (PRD R-17, closed).

get.description:
The latest version a reader may see: a clinician who treats the patient sees the
draft too; the patient sees the latest signed version, without clinician-only notes.

put.description:
Create or update the visit's draft note. Saved as the clinician goes; signing is
separate, and a signed note is amended, never edited.

post.description: End the session this access token belongs to. Its refresh token dies with it.
End every session of the caller's login, on every device.

Spend a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token.

Needs no access token: refreshing is what a client does once its access token has
expired. A spent refresh token presented again ends the session.

get.description: Liveness probe. The test stack and the first case both assert on it.

The newest error traces across the services, each reduced to its root operation,
first failed step and message, with a link to the trace.

Every process's liveness, the critical flows, backlogs and AI health over the last
`hours` (1, 6 or 24), in plain statuses with a reason each.

post.description: Queue a message to one patient: the patient's email if they have one, else SMS.

get.description: Declared before /{patient_id}: otherwise FastAPI parses "me" as a UUID and 422s.

post.description:
Upload a report: the request body is the file (PDF, PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB). The
patient for themselves, front desk and the treating provider on their behalf. The type
is read from the bytes, not trusted from the name. Text is extracted afterwards.

get.description:
A document and its extracted text, for the patient and the treating clinician --
what the assistant reads to explain or summarise a report (spec 9.1).

post.description: The ordering clinician marks an uploaded result reviewed.

get.description:
Name, email and role for the given login ids -- admin only.

For pages that hold user ids from elsewhere, like the assistant's usage page (its
records carry only the token's subject): the admin's browser joins them, so the
assistant never reads Part A's users. Unknown ids are simply absent from the answer.
